question: to the Commission Jorge Buxadé Villalba (PfE) Subject:

Spain’s Under-Secretariat of Foreign Affairs, the European Union and Cooperation awarded file 2024SWs0014, for EUR 1 131 295.68 (plus VAT), to Cuban state entity PALCO for staff reinforcements at the Spanish consulate in Havana for the processing of citizenship applications in application of what is known as the ‘grandchildren’s law’1. According to press reports, the contract was awarded through a restricted procedure with a single tender and no reduction in the budget. Cuba is not a party to the WTO Agreement on Government Procurement, and the Political Dialogue and Cooperation Agreement between the EU and Cuba does not integrate Cuba into the European public procurement market, nor does it provide for equivalent reciprocal opening of the market. In addition, a Cuban stateowned company may have received foreign financial contributions within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560. In light of the above: 1.
Did Spain inform the Commission about this contract, in accordance with the duty of sincere cooperation (Article 4(3) of the Treaty on European Union ) and Regulation (EU) 2022/2560?

Does the Commission view the absence of an EU-Cuba public procurement agreement as precluding the presumption of reciprocity for the purposes of Article 68 of Spain’s Public Sector Contracts Law (LCSP)?
What view does the Commission take of employees of a state company of the Cuban regime having access to applicants’ sensitive personal data?
Eighth additional provision of Spanish Law 20/2022 of 19 October 2022 on democratic memory: https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2022-17099. 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.9.2026) Spain’s Under-Secretariat of Foreign Affairs did not inform the Commission of the award of file 2024SWs0014 (the contract). Under Article 28(1)(a) of the Foreign Subsidies Regulation (FSR)1, a foreign financial contribution in public procurement is notifiable where the estimated contract value, net of Value Added Tax, is at least EUR 250 million. The contract did not reach that threshold. Therefore, no notification was required under Article 29 of the FSR, and, consequently, none was required pursuant to Article 4(3) of the Treaty on European Union2 either. Cuba is neither a Party to the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement3 – which would otherwise apply to the case mentioned by the Honourable Member – nor does it have any bilateral agreement with the EU on public procurement. Therefore, national contracting authorities are still allowed to award contracts to Cuban bidders, since there is currently no EU provision forbidding it. Indeed, according to the principles established in the Kolin judgment of the Court of Justice of the EU4, it is for the individual contracting authority, and not its Member State, to decide whether or not third country bidders can participate in a procurement procedure in the absence of any international agreement guaranteeing that right. Transfers of personal data to third countries may be carried out only in compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)5. The GDPR sets a governance system which tasks national supervisory authorities to ensure its monitoring and enforcement. Thus, the Spanish data protection authority would seem the competent one to ensure compliance with it, including the processing of applicants’ sensitive personal data.
1 Regulation (EU) 2022/2560 of 14 December 2022 on foreign subsidies distorting the internal market,

https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2560/oj. 2 Treaty on European Union, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/treaty/teu_2016/oj/eng. 3 World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement, https://www.wto.org/english/docs_e/legal_e/rev-gpr-94_01_e.pdf. 4 Judgment of 22 October 2024, Kolin Inşaat Turizm Sanayi ve Ticaret AȘ v Državna komisija za kontrolu postupaka javne nabave, C-652/22, EU:C:2024:910, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:62022CJ0652. 5 Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data, and repealing Directive 95/46/EC, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng.
